quotes.text: Real agency isn't about writing better prompts. It starts with structure. It requires a system that actually knows who you are, how you work, and what matters to your business.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the episode's core thesis that structure, not prompting, creates agency.

quotes.text: An action layer without memory is dangerous because you end up with a system that can do things without knowing when it should.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains concisely why memory must come before autonomous action.

quotes.text: Skills are permanent. They live inside your system as versioned, reusable, and discoverable assets. Every time you invoke a skill, you aren't re-instructing the system on how to do a job
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clearly distinguishes reusable skills from one-off prompts.

quotes.text: Trusting the system means you assume the model will fail at some point. You build safety into the architecture and design the process so that failures are caught before they cause real damage.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Offers a practical governance principle for agentic systems.

quotes.text: Human feedback is the only thing that prevents an automated system from drifting away from your original intent.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes human review as a core feature rather than a failure of automation.

takeaways: Copilot becomes an operating system only when memory, action, reasoning and governance are layered into one architecture.
Reusable skill files, Copilot Cowork and agent flows turn one-off prompts into orchestrated, governed workflows grounded in Microsoft Graph data.
Start with one high-friction workflow, test against real historical cases, keep humans in the loop and budget for engineering, not just licenses.
hook: Most people use Copilot as a smart stranger that forgets everything after each chat. This episode is for Microsoft 365 architects and power users who want to turn Copilot into a Jarvis-style system with persistent memory, skills, Copilot Cowork, agent flows, Graph grounding and governance, and who need a realistic build plan.
